newsitem.title: USA: FSI sees fiscal '97 sales 15-20 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: FSI sees fiscal '97 sales 15-20 pct lower.

text.p: FSI International Inc said Tuesday it expects to post fiscal 1997 sales 15 to 20 percent lower than the $304 million reported in fiscal 1996.
The company said it expects to report its lowest sales for the year for its current third quarter.

"(W)e expect the third quarter to be our low point for sales in fiscal 1997 and we are now forecasting fiscal year 1997 sales to be 15 to 20 percent below the $304 million fiscal 1996 level," Joel Elftmann, chairman and chief executive of FSI, said in a statement.
FSI reported earnings for its second quarter ended March 1 of $0.08 a share versus $0.37 for the quarter last year. Sales were $60.16 million compared with $75.43 million.
For the first six months of fiscal 1997, FSI had earnings of $0.26 a share on sales of $127.15 million versus $0.70 a share on $145.78 million in sales.

"The lower earnings in the second quarter and first half of fiscal 1997, as compared to the same periods in fiscal 1996, were due to reduced sales, primarily related to the semiconductor equipment industry slowdown and a lower gross margin percentage," the company said.
The lower gross margin was the result of a change in the product sales mix, increased product warranty costs and lower utilization of manufacturing capacity, FSI said.
Nonetheless, FSI said order activity increased for the quarter, and its book-to-bill ratio, which measures new orders over shipments, was greater than 1.0.
"This reinforces our belief that industry conditions are improving," Elftmann said. "We expect further improvement in bookings in the third quarter of fiscal 1997."
Elftmann said FSI's future is "very promising" citing competitive products, facility expansion programs and product and process development programs.

"We believe that we are well positioned for the expected industry upturn," Elftmann said. "If industry conditions continue to improve and our new products and process applications gain customer acceptance as we expect, we believe our fiscal 1998 sales will meet or exceed the fiscal 1996 sales level of $304 million."
